title: Grateful Dead Live at Veterans' Memorial Coliseum on 1982-09-23
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Samplitude Professional v11.03 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1982 show with a smoking Wheel→Other One→Wharf Rat sequence and an electrifying Althea.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean soundboard mix (Charlie Miller’s work) that brings out the band’s tight interplay, especially Brent’s B3 work and a surprisingly present Phil bass. Musically the show bursts with energy – the Wheel‑Other One‑Wharf Rat suite, a five‑star Althea, standout Mexicali Blues and a rousing Johnny B. Goode make it one of the era’s highlights.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate 4‑5 stars, praising both performance and recording; only a single low‑star comment focuses on Bob's slide, so the overall combined show/recording quality is judged very good.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp board mix with solid instrument balance; Brent’s B3 is prominent and Phil’s bass sits better than typical for the era. Minor tape‑transfer speed quirks noted by one reviewer, but no major dropouts or muddiness.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set flows seamlessly, with the Wheel→Other One→Wharf Rat suite leading into a powerful Althea and ending on an upbeat Johnny B. Goode.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers note Jerry’s playing is “on”, electric, and his vocals/strings are strong throughout, especially on Althea.
band_member_comments.Phil: Generally low in the mix for this era, but this board brings out more Phil than usual; praised for solid bass presence.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob’s slide work on Althea sparked debate – one reviewer called it awful early‑'82 but acknowledges improvement and adds to the song’s impact here.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent (keyboards) is highlighted for laying down a strong B3 foundation throughout the show.
